name: Van Hilleary
primary_label: Republican Primary · U.S. House TN-6 (Open Seat)
bio: Former four-term U.S. Rep and 2002 GOP gubernatorial nominee. Was Rose's chief of staff, bringing D.C. experience to the open primary.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Van Hilleary supports President Trump's education freedom agenda and parental rights, emphasizing reducing federal agency interference in local schools. No specific public positions on pre-K, Head Start, or childcare costs were found.
early_childhood_ed.details: Hilleary's 2026 campaign website lists among his policy positions: 'Champion parents' rights and support President Trump's education freedom agenda at every turn' and 'Push back hard on federal agency interference in local schools, businesses, and communities.' His iVoterGuide profile notes support for eliminating the U.S. Department of Education and returning control to states and communities. During his prior congressional service (1995–2002), he supported rural school district grants. No statements on pre-K, Head Start, childcare subsidies, or early childhood programs were found in his 2025–2026 campaign materials.

child_hunger.summary: No public position found as of July 2026 on child hunger, SNAP, school meals, or food assistance programs.
child_hunger.details: No public statements on child hunger, SNAP/food stamps, school meals, WIC, food banks, or food insecurity were found for Van Hilleary as of July 2026. His affordability platform focuses on reducing spending, cutting regulations, and opposing tax hikes as the path to family affordability. Hilleary served as chief of staff to Rep. John Rose, who voted YES on the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, but no separate statement from Hilleary himself on that legislation was found.

parental_support.summary: Van Hilleary frames family economic support through broad tax-cut and spending-reduction principles rather than specific parental support programs. His historical record includes voting to expand the Child Tax Credit in 2001.
parental_support.details: Hilleary's current campaign does not include specific positions on paid family leave, childcare subsidies, or the Child Tax Credit. His 'Affordability' platform calls for supporting Trump's spending cuts, slashing job-killing regulations, backing energy independence, and opposing tax hikes. During his prior congressional service (1995–2002), records show he voted YES on reducing the marriage tax by doubling the child tax credit (HR 6, March 2001). He also signed the Contract with America, which included the Families Reinforcement Act covering child support enforcement, tax incentives for adoption, and an elderly dependent care tax credit. His 2026 campaign emphasizes 'parents raising their kids according to their values' and opposes government overreach into family decisions.

name: Johnny Garrett
primary_label: Republican Primary · U.S. House TN-6 (Open Seat)
bio: State legislator from Goodlettsville. First to file petitions; raised $1.1M with $1M+ cash on hand. Strong grassroots support.

early_childhood_ed.summary: As Tennessee House Republican Whip, Garrett was associated with a 2026 session that expanded Education Freedom Scholarships and raised teacher pay, but no specific positions on pre-K, Head Start, or childcare access were found in his congressional campaign materials.
early_childhood_ed.details: Garrett's April 2026 Capitol Report highlights education wins from the session he helped shepherd: expanding Education Freedom Scholarships from 20,000 to 35,000 students (HB 2532/SB 2247), raising the minimum starting teacher salary to $50,000, and adding $339 million in new recurring K-12 education dollars. The session also limited screen time in elementary classrooms. These are K-12 focused. His congressional campaign website emphasizes he is running to 'stand up for conservative family values.' He serves on the Children & Family Affairs Subcommittee in the Tennessee House. No specific positions on pre-K access, Head Start, federal childcare tax credits, or childcare affordability were found in his 2026 congressional campaign materials.

child_hunger.summary: No specific public position found on child hunger, SNAP, school meals, or food assistance programs as of July 2026.
child_hunger.details: No public statements on child hunger, SNAP, school meals, WIC, food banks, or food insecurity were found in Garrett's 2026 congressional campaign materials. His April 2026 legislative recap mentions strengthened protections for 'vulnerable adults and children' in general terms. The Tennessee legislative session he helped pass did not fully fund the Summer EBT bill, allocating $7 million for S-EBT beginning in 2027 as a compromise. No record of Garrett personally sponsoring or publicly backing child nutrition bills was found.

parental_support.summary: Garrett frames himself as a champion of conservative family values and parental rights. His 2026 Tennessee legislative session included a new caregiver support pilot program and Safe Haven Law expansion, though no specific positions on paid family leave or childcare subsidies were found.
parental_support.details: Garrett's February 2026 Capitol Report notes two family-support measures advanced in the session: the Safe Haven Law expansion (HB 1844) to include ambulance stations as approved newborn surrender locations, and a parental consent protection bill (HB 1665) limiting health care providers from asking minors gender identity questions without parental presence and consent. His April 2026 session recap also highlights creation of a 3-year pilot program to support caregivers' lost wages and expenses (HB 1443/SB 1777). His congressional campaign website positions him as running for 'conservative family values.' He has three children of his own and his wife is a registered nurse. No specific positions on paid family leave or childcare subsidies at the federal level were found.

name: Dale Braden
primary_label: Republican Primary · U.S. House TN-6 (Open Seat)
bio: Republican primary candidate. Campaign suspended — confirmed by Tennessee Conservative News; campaign website is offline.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Campaign suspended. No public position found on early childhood education, childcare, or pre-K as of July 2026.
early_childhood_ed.details: Dale Braden ran as a Republican candidate for Tennessee's 7th Congressional District but suspended his campaign. He subsequently filed as an American Independent Conservative Party candidate for the general election with minimal fundraising ($235 in contributions). No public statements on early childhood education, childcare, Head Start, or pre-K were found for Braden in any campaign materials.

child_hunger.summary: Campaign suspended. No public position found on child hunger, SNAP, or food assistance as of July 2026.
child_hunger.details: No public statements on child hunger, SNAP/food stamps, school meals, WIC, food banks, or food insecurity were found for Dale Braden as of July 2026. Braden's campaign was characterized by early activity in the region but no policy statements on child nutrition programs were recorded in available sources. His campaign suspension in October 2025 and subsequent limited re-engagement produced no detailed policy platform.

parental_support.summary: Campaign suspended. No public position found on parental support, paid family leave, or Child Tax Credit as of July 2026.
parental_support.details: No public statements on paid family leave, Child Tax Credit, childcare subsidies, parental rights legislation, or family economic support were found for Dale Braden as of July 2026. In announcing his initial suspension in October 2025, Braden stated: 'Faith in God, love of family, and loyalty to our Constitution aren't just political positions, they are the very foundation of my life,' indicating general conservative family values, but no specific policy positions on parental support programs were articulated.

name: Mike Croley
primary_label: Democratic Primary · U.S. House TN-6 (Open Seat)
bio: Democratic candidate facing a steep climb in this strongly Republican district.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Croley has stated that Tennessee's schools are underfunded and that he supports fully funding education, but no specific public positions on pre-K, Head Start, or childcare access were found in his 2025–2026 campaign materials.
early_childhood_ed.details: Mike Croley is the Democratic candidate for Tennessee's 6th Congressional District. In his campaign bio and website, he states he is running because 'our schools are underfunded' and cites his role as a devoted father. His 'AAA Blueprint' campaign platform focuses on Affordability, Access, and Accountability. His Nashville Banner candidate questionnaire (July 2026) includes his support for 'tuition-free universities' and expresses concern about underfunded schools but does not detail specific early childhood education policy positions such as pre-K funding, Head Start expansion, or childcare tax credits.

child_hunger.summary: Croley explicitly supports fully funding SNAP, WIC, food banks, and similar programs as part of his cost-of-living platform.
child_hunger.details: In his Nashville Banner candidate questionnaire (July 2026), Croley directly states the policies he would support to alleviate cost-of-living increases include: 'fully funding SNAP, WIC, food banks and other similar programs.' This is among the most specific child hunger-related policy positions found across the TN-6 and TN-7 candidates. He also supports raising the federal minimum wage to $20 per hour. His campaign blog post 'The Affordability Crisis Is a Healthcare Crisis' (April 2026) discusses how the One Big Beautiful Bill Act ended enhanced federal premium tax credits and argues that 'working families in Tennessee's 6th District are getting steamrolled.' As a former USDA rotational assignment employee and Navy veteran, he has described direct experience with public service programs serving families.

parental_support.summary: Croley supports universal basic healthcare, raising the minimum wage, and fully funding family assistance programs, which he frames as essential support for families with children. No specific positions on paid family leave or Child Tax Credit were found.
parental_support.details: Croley's Nashville Banner questionnaire lists his key policy priorities including: fully funding SNAP, WIC, and food banks; raising the federal minimum wage to $20/hour with tiered implementation for small businesses; and supporting 'universal basic healthcare.' He states: 'Much more, I fully support universal basic healthcare. When I was in the military, we had a version of universal basic healthcare. I didn't pay for doctor appointments or prescriptions. We have the money, we don't have the values.' He describes himself as 'a husband, a father' and someone who will fight for working families. No specific positions on paid family leave, Child Tax Credit, or childcare subsidies were found.

name: Matt Van Epps
bio: Won the December 2025 special election after Mark Green's resignation. West Point graduate, combat veteran, and former state commissioner.

early_childhood_ed.summary: As TN-7 incumbent since December 2025, Van Epps strongly supports school choice, voucher programs, and eliminating the U.S. Department of Education. No specific positions on pre-K, Head Start, or childcare costs were found.
early_childhood_ed.details: Matt Van Epps was elected to the TN-7 seat in a December 4, 2025 special election. In his iVoterGuide candidate questionnaire, he responded 'Strongly Agree' to: 'I support school choice, including voucher programs, tax credits, charter schools, private schools, and home schools' and 'I support eliminating the U.S. Department of Education and giving control back to states and communities.' His campaign website lists 'Champion School Choice' as a core agenda item. No specific positions on pre-K funding, Head Start, or childcare access were found in his congressional or campaign materials as of July 2026.

child_hunger.summary: Van Epps stated in a pre-election questionnaire that he 'would have voted for the Big Beautiful Bill,' which included significant SNAP cuts affecting child nutrition. No direct statements on child hunger programs or school meals were found.
child_hunger.details: Van Epps was not yet in Congress when the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1) passed the House on May 22, 2025. In his iVoterGuide candidate questionnaire, he stated: 'I would have voted for the Big Beautiful Bill, now Law, which has provided the biggest tax cuts in American history. I stand with the President in these efforts.' This bill included significant SNAP cuts. Tennessee advocates warned the law could cost the state over $110 million annually and affect hundreds of thousands of Tennesseans. His subsequent voting record shows no bills directly related to child hunger. No public statements specifically addressing child hunger, food banks, or school meals were found from Van Epps as of July 2026.

parental_support.summary: Van Epps emphasizes school choice, conservative family values, and protecting children from what he describes as harmful gender ideology. No specific positions on paid family leave, Child Tax Credit, or childcare subsidies were found.
parental_support.details: In his iVoterGuide questionnaire, Van Epps responded 'Strongly Agree' to: 'Children are the most vulnerable members of society and must be protected from abuse, including gender ideology, grooming, and bodily mutilation.' He also states he 'will promote families and a culture of life' as part of his pro-life position. His campaign website includes 'Fighting for Tennessee Families' and 'Champion School Choice.' His Labor scorecard shows he failed to cosponsor national paid family and medical leave for all workers (H.R. 5390) and failed to cosponsor establishing a national paid sick days standard (H.R. 7531), consistent with Republican caucus norms. No specific positions on the Child Tax Credit or childcare subsidies were found.

name: David Kustoff
bio: Five-term incumbent attorney. Unopposed in Republican primary; $2.8M cash on hand.

early_childhood_ed.summary: No specific public statements on pre-K access or Head Start funding were found for Rep. Kustoff in 2025-2026. As a Ways and Means Committee member, he supported the One Big Beautiful Bill Act which expanded 529 education savings accounts to cover K-12 materials.
early_childhood_ed.details: Rep. David Kustoff (R, TN-8) sits on the House Ways and Means Committee and was a key architect of the tax provisions in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, signed into law on July 4, 2025. The bill expanded 529 education savings accounts to allow families to use them for K-12 educational materials and postsecondary trades credentials. No specific statements from Kustoff on Head Start funding, pre-K access, or federal childcare subsidies were located in the sources reviewed. The bill also expanded the child and dependent care credit and flexible spending accounts (FSAs) for childcare, which Kustoff defended as beneficial to working families.

child_hunger.summary: Rep. Kustoff voted in favor of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act in May 2025, which cut approximately $186-267 billion from SNAP over the next decade and added new work requirements. He defended the bill as ensuring SNAP works efficiently.
child_hunger.details: Kustoff voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which passed the House 215-214 on May 22, 2025, and was signed into law on July 4, 2025. The law cut an estimated $186-267 billion from SNAP and imposed new work requirements on recipients ages 55-64, among other categories. By May 2026, approximately 100,000 Tennesseans had lost SNAP benefits since July 2025. Protesters gathered outside Kustoff's Memphis office on May 28, 2025. Kustoff's office responded: 'As a member of the House Ways and Means Committee... Congressman Kustoff played a key role in crafting the tax portion of the One Big, Beautiful Bill... this legislation will also... ensure Medicaid & SNAP work efficiently for Americans.' No public statements were found from Kustoff supporting increased federal food assistance for children.

parental_support.summary: Rep. Kustoff was a lead advocate for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which permanently expanded the Child Tax Credit to $2,200 per child and made permanent the paid leave tax credit for small businesses.
parental_support.details: As a senior member of the House Ways and Means Committee, Kustoff championed the tax provisions of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. In a June 2025 op-ed, he wrote that the bill would boost 'the doubled child tax credit' and help families avoid a '26% tax hike.' The bill raised the Child Tax Credit from $2,000 to $2,200 per child for more than 40 million families, made the paid leave tax credit for small businesses permanent, expanded the child and dependent care credit, and grew FSA limits. He did not publicly support paid family leave as a direct government benefit or childcare subsidies outside the tax code framework.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Dewey Gordon Bryan (who campaigns as Gordon Bryan), the Democratic TN-8 primary candidate, supports a major increase in federal education spending, including significant investment in rural schools.
early_childhood_ed.details: Dewey Gordon Bryan — whose legal name is Dewey Gordon Bryan, though he campaigns as Gordon Bryan — is a retired U.S. Navy aviator and FedEx pilot running in the TN-8 Democratic primary on August 6, 2026. According to his BallotReady profile, Bryan 'proposes a major increase in federal education spending, including significant investment in rural schools, real increases in teacher pay, and directing the Department of Education to send federal grants straight to school systems rather than through the states.' No specific statements on pre-K, Head Start, or childcare access were found.

child_hunger.summary: Bryan lists 'SNAP benefits' and 'Medicaid' as policy areas he is personally passionate about, and he criticized the One Big Beautiful Bill Act for taking 'food and health care away from' constituents.
child_hunger.details: In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, Bryan listed 'Economy, affordability, Social Security, health care, SNAP benefits, Medicaid, AND EVERYTHING ELSE republican representatives are against' as areas of personal policy passion. He stated one of his three key campaign messages was that David Kustoff 'helped write the 1BBB that has screwed over hundreds of thousands OF HIS OWN CONSTITUENTS,' pointing to constituents having to 'choose between purchasing food for their families or medication for themselves.' No specific legislative proposals on school meals, SNAP expansion, WIC, or food banks were found in his campaign materials as of July 2026.

parental_support.summary: Bryan supports Medicare for All as his healthcare approach, and broadly supports affordability measures, but no specific public positions on Child Tax Credit, paid family leave, or childcare subsidies were found in his campaign materials.
parental_support.details: Bryan's BallotReady profile states his 'approach to health care comes down to one phrase: Medicare for all.' His broader campaign platform focuses on economic affordability, Social Security preservation, and reversal of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's impacts. He has not published specific positions on paid family leave, Child Tax Credit reforms, or childcare subsidies as of July 2026.

name: Leonard Perkins
bio: Democratic primary candidate. Pastor and substance abuse counselor with 23 years of community service.

early_childhood_ed.summary: No specific public position on early childhood education or childcare was found for Leonard Perkins as of July 2026. His campaign website focuses on veterans' rights, women's rights, and organized labor.
early_childhood_ed.details: Leonard Perkins Sr. is a Memphis pastor, retired U.S. Air Force air traffic controller, and substance abuse counselor running in the TN-8 Democratic primary on August 6, 2026. His campaign website (perkinstocongress.com) lists his top priorities as 'Veteran's Rights, Women's Rights, Pro Labor,' as well as voting rights, student debt, small businesses, and broader democratic concerns. In a January 2026 interview with The Jackson Post, he stated: 'I think the measuring stick for a society is how it treats its babies, seniors, veterans and women. We can be doing a much better job of all those things, so I want to raise the bar for District 8.' No specific positions on pre-K access, Head Start, childcare costs, or early learning programs were found in available sources.

child_hunger.summary: Leonard Perkins has stated broadly that the current representative 'takes money out of our pockets, food out of our children's mouths,' signaling concern about federal cuts to nutrition programs, but no specific policy proposals on SNAP or child hunger were found.
child_hunger.details: In his January 2026 campaign launch interview in The Jackson Post, Perkins said of incumbent Rep. Kustoff: 'When they do that, he takes opportunities away from our people here. He takes money out of our pockets, food out of our children's mouths and resources away from our veterans who have served our country.' This suggests opposition to federal cuts affecting food access for families, consistent with criticism of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's SNAP reductions. However, no specific legislative proposals on SNAP, free school meals, WIC, Summer EBT, or food banks were located in his campaign materials or public statements as of July 2026.

parental_support.summary: Perkins's platform emphasizes women's rights (including reproductive autonomy) and organized labor, which relate indirectly to parental support, but no specific positions on Child Tax Credit, paid family leave, or childcare subsidies were found.
parental_support.details: Leonard Perkins's campaign platform centers on veterans' rights, women's reproductive autonomy, and organized labor. His 2024 Tennessean questionnaire (from a prior run) listed top priorities as returning 'reproductive autonomy to women, streamline the veterans benefits process, voting rights, protect organized labor.' His 2026 campaign materials did not include specific positions on paid family leave, Child Tax Credit, childcare subsidies, or maternal health programs. He stated his general philosophy as: 'I think the measuring stick for a society is how it treats its babies, seniors, veterans and women.'

early_childhood_ed.summary: Pamela Moses's seven-point platform includes youth engagement and mentorship programs, but no specific positions on pre-K, Head Start, or childcare access were found in her public materials as of July 2026.
early_childhood_ed.details: Pamela Moses is an independent candidate running for Tennessee's 8th Congressional District. Her seven-point policy plan includes under 'Community Health and Wellness': 'Youth Engagement Programs: Developing mentorship and leadership programs for youth that build critical skills such as entrepreneurship, problem-solving, and teamwork, empowering the next generation.' No specific mentions of pre-K, Head Start funding, childcare costs, or early childhood education programs were found.

child_hunger.summary: Pamela Moses includes 'Food Security and Local Agriculture' as one of her seven policy pillars, with a focus on eliminating food deserts and supporting farmers' markets in underserved communities.
child_hunger.details: Moses's policy platform includes a dedicated section on 'Food Security and Local Agriculture' in which she plans to 'eliminate food deserts in Tennessee and promote sustainable agriculture' by: (1) 'Supporting Farmers' Markets: Encouraging the establishment of farmers' markets in underserved areas and providing direct channels for local farmers to sell their produce'; and (2) 'Community Engagement: Promoting educational programs that teach people how to grow their own food and make healthy dietary choices, contributing to community health and food security.' No specific positions on SNAP, WIC, free school meals, or federal child nutrition programs were stated.

parental_support.summary: Moses advocates for universal healthcare access including mental health investment, but no specific positions on Child Tax Credit, paid family leave, or childcare subsidies were found.
parental_support.details: Moses's campaign platform under 'Healthcare for All' advocates for 'Mental Health Investment: Expanding mental health resources, particularly in underserved communities' and 'Rehabilitation over Incarceration.' Her 'Community Health and Wellness' plank also includes youth mentorship programs. No specific positions on paid family leave, Child Tax Credit, childcare subsidies, or maternal health programs were found in her public campaign materials as of July 2026.

name: Horace Taylor
bio: Independent candidate. Describes himself as 'progressive in thought, yet grounded in principles and values.' $0 in FEC-reported contributions.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Horace Taylor lists 'education and public safety' among his policy passions, but no specific positions on pre-K, Head Start, childcare, or early learning programs were found in his public materials as of July 2026.
early_childhood_ed.details: Horace Taylor is an independent candidate for Tennessee's 8th Congressional District, a retired Army Major and cybersecurity professional. In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, he listed 'education and public safety' as one area of public policy he is personally passionate about, alongside cost of living, rural healthcare, agricultural policy, and closing the broadband gap. His campaign website (horacetaylortn.com) does not include a specific section on early childhood education, childcare access, Head Start, or pre-K programs.

child_hunger.summary: No specific public position on child hunger, SNAP, school meals, or food insecurity programs was found for Horace Taylor as of July 2026.
child_hunger.details: Taylor's campaign website and Ballotpedia survey responses do not include specific positions on SNAP, child nutrition programs, free school meals, Summer EBT, WIC, or food banks. His three main campaign priorities are: (1) immediate tariff relief for West Tennessee farmers; (2) affordable and accessible healthcare; and (3) full support for service members and veterans. No public statements connecting Taylor to the Tennessee Summer EBT or SNAP debates of 2025-2026 were located.

parental_support.summary: No specific public positions on Child Tax Credit, paid family leave, childcare subsidies, or parental support programs were found for Horace Taylor as of July 2026.
parental_support.details: Taylor describes himself as 'progressive in thought, yet grounded in principles and values' and as an independent not bound by party loyalty. His vision page emphasizes healthcare affordability and protection of Medicare and Medicaid from cuts. No specific statements on paid family leave, Child Tax Credit, childcare subsidies, or maternal health programs were located in his campaign materials or public statements.

name: Steve Cohen
bio: Memphis-area Democratic congressman serving since 2007. Announced May 15, 2026 he would not seek reelection after redistricting dismantled TN-9, but left the door open if legal challenges succeed. cohenforcongress.com remains active and he cosponsored the Universal School Meals Program Act of 2026 (H.R. 8798) in May 2026.
status_line: Conditional retirement announced May 15, 2026 · Active if redistricting lawsuit succeeds

early_childhood_ed.summary: Rep. Cohen has consistently championed Head Start funding for Shelby County and worked for decades to expand pre-K access, most recently announcing a $7.4 million Head Start grant to the Shelby County Board of Education in April 2025.
early_childhood_ed.details: Steve Cohen has a long record on early childhood education. In Congress, he regularly secured Head Start grants for the Shelby County Board of Education, including a $7,446,186 grant in April 2025 (covering programs January through June 2025), a $13.3 million grant in December 2022, and a $12.9 million supplemental grant in May 2022. He cosponsored H.R. 8654 (reauthorize Nita M. Lowey Community Learning Centers program for 2026–2035). His statement: 'Head Start is an investment in our community, its children and our future.' In March 2026, Cohen defended public education for migrant children, opposing a state directive to remove immigrant children from Children's Special Services programs. He voted NO on the One Big Beautiful Bill (H.R.1) in both May and July 2025.

child_hunger.summary: Rep. Cohen has been one of the most vocal advocates for child food security in Tennessee, writing letters to Gov. Lee urging Summer EBT participation and voting against the 2025 reconciliation bill's $300 billion in SNAP and school meals cuts.
child_hunger.details: Cohen repeatedly pressed Tennessee's governor to accept federal food assistance funding. In December 2025 he wrote Gov. Lee urging Summer EBT application before the January 1, 2026 deadline, noting the prior year's opt-out forfeited roughly $84 million that could have fed approximately 700,000 Tennessee children. He wrote: 'There is no good reason to turn down aid for hungry children.' He voted NO on the One Big Beautiful Bill (May and July 2025), which he described as containing 'the largest reduction to health care and nutritional assistance in our country's history' including a $300 billion cut to SNAP and school meals that he said would put '18 million children at risk of losing meals.' His district analysis noted the bill would 'take food off tables of 62,000 households in Memphis who rely on SNAP.' He also cosponsored H.R. 8246 (expand SNAP to college students) and H.R. 8055 (extend WIC for new moms).

parental_support.summary: Rep. Cohen cosponsored the FAMILY Act of 2025 to create a permanent national paid family leave program and introduced the NEWBORN Act to reduce infant mortality, while consistently opposing legislation cutting the Child Tax Credit or Medicaid for families.
parental_support.details: Cohen's Children and Families page states he 'has pushed for paid family leave and has continuously cosponsored the Family and Medical Insurance Leave (FAMILY) Act.' Congressional records confirm he cosponsored the FAMILY Act of 2025 in September 2025. In March 2025, Cohen reintroduced the NEWBORN Act, establishing infant-mortality-focused pilot programs in highest-risk areas. Cohen's office also announced Healthy Marriage and Responsible Fatherhood grants totaling approximately $1.98 million to Le Bonheur Community Health and Agape Child and Family Services in September 2025. He voted NO on the 2025 reconciliation bill, noting Democrats filed amendments to expand the Child Tax Credit that Republicans rejected. In June 2026, he wrote to Gov. Lee calling it 'morally repulsive' to report sick immigrant children in Children's Special Services to immigration enforcement.

name: Justin J. Pearson
bio: Progressive challenger known for the Byhalia Pipeline fight and the 2023 'Tennessee Three' gun-protest expulsion. Pledging no corporate PAC money; raised $374K in Q1 2026 alone, narrowly outraising Cohen that quarter. Justice Democrats endorsed; pledged $1M through Leaders We Deserve. ⚠ The new map signed May 7 dismantles the Memphis-based TN-9; Pearson's brother KeShaun was arrested protesting at the Capitol. All candidates must refile by May 15; Pearson's campaign path in the redrawn district is unclear pending legal challenges.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Pearson's congressional campaign platform calls for robust investment in public education and opposing school vouchers, though he has not published specific early childhood education or pre-K policy proposals as of July 2026.
early_childhood_ed.details: Justin J. Pearson's campaign issues page states: 'Education is the most important investment we can make in our young people. We need to make sure every child has the tools to be successful in college or in careers by bringing back trades into school, as well as ensuring every school has the equipment and tools to educate children.' He calls for 'demanding more funding to Title I schools' and pledges to 'work to pass a national law that ends private school vouchers which serve as welfare checks for the wealthy.' He supports a national law guaranteeing annual public school teacher pay increases. His campaign platforms center primarily on poverty reduction and K-12 public school investment rather than early childhood programs specifically. No specific statements on Head Start, pre-K, or childcare programs were found as of July 2026.

child_hunger.summary: Pearson prominently centers child poverty and food security — 33% of District 9 children live below the poverty line — and proposes doubling the EITC, cutting grocery taxes, and increasing the minimum wage as anti-hunger tools.
child_hunger.details: Pearson's campaign platform highlights that 33% of children in TN-9 live below the poverty line. From a July 2026 interview: 'I'm not going to be supporting the sending of billions in bombs overseas, when people in my own district—their houses are sinking, and their kids are hungry. It always amazes me that America will always find billions and billions to fight wars, but won't do anything like that to fight poverty and hunger.' His platform proposes doubling the Earned Income Tax Credit ('would lift half of children in the country out of poverty'), cutting taxes on working-class people and ending the grocery tax, and increasing the minimum wage county-by-county using the MIT Living Wage Calculator. He endorses taxing the highest-income earners to fund these programs. No specific SNAP or school meals legislative proposals were found by name in his platform.

parental_support.summary: Pearson's platform supports Medicare for All, guaranteed basic income, minimum wage increases, and protecting immigrant families with children, but has not published specific paid family leave or Child Tax Credit positions as of July 2026.
parental_support.details: Pearson's campaign platform addresses several areas intersecting with parental support. On healthcare, he supports Medicare for All, which he says would cover 'reproductive health.' He also supports 'guaranteed basic income programs for poor people and people impacted by job loss due to automation.' He calls for minimum wage increases framed as essential to lift families out of poverty. He commits to 'fighting against the separation of children and their families' and defending Dreamers. His campaign has endorsements from Bernie Sanders, AOC, the Working Families Party, and Justice Democrats. No specific positions on the federal FAMILY Act, Child Tax Credit, paid family leave legislation, or childcare subsidies in campaign materials were found as of July 2026.

name: Charlotte Bergmann
bio: Republican nominee in a D+35 district.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Bergmann supports school choice — 'Parents have the absolute right to choose their child's education whether public, private, charter, or homeschool' — but has no publicly stated position on early childhood education, pre-K, Head Start, or childcare access.
early_childhood_ed.details: Charlotte Bergmann's campaign website focuses on law and order, economic affordability, border security, and school choice at the K-12 level. Her BallotReady profile states: 'Parents have the absolute right to choose their child's education whether public, private, charter, or homeschool.' Her older campaign site lists 'Enhance Memphis Labor Force' as a priority, noting she is 'pro-school choice, where parents can make their own decisions about their child's education' and plans to 'put vocational classes back in the high schools.' She also supports expanding trade school options and internship programs. No public statements on early childhood programs, Head Start, childcare costs, or pre-K access were found.

child_hunger.summary: No public position on child hunger, SNAP, school meals, Summer EBT, WIC, or related food assistance programs was found in Bergmann's campaign materials as of July 2026.
child_hunger.details: Bergmann's campaign website and available voter guide profiles do not include any statements on SNAP, school meal programs, Summer EBT, WIC, food banks, or child food insecurity. Her platform focuses on crime reduction, economic development, school choice, healthcare reform, and veterans' issues. Her general economic platform favors 'less regulation and lower taxes' and private-sector-led solutions.
